Conditional LATE from externally supplied nuisance predictions

Source: R/user-dnn-clate.R
clate_dnn.Rd

An augmented binary-IV estimator with rich adjustment and reduced-dimensional reporting. Nuisance functions are supplied as aligned predictions; the estimator fits no learners.

Usage

clate_dnn(
  data = NULL,
  x_cols = NULL,
  y_col = NULL,
  d_col = NULL,
  a_col = NULL,
  e_col = NULL,
  m_y0_col = NULL,
  m_y1_col = NULL,
  m_d0_col = NULL,
  m_d1_col = NULL,
  X = NULL,
  X0 = NULL,
  x0 = NULL,
  Y = NULL,
  D = NULL,
  A = NULL,
  e = NULL,
  m_y0 = NULL,
  m_y1 = NULL,
  m_d0 = NULL,
  m_d1 = NULL,
  clip = 1e-08,
  one_sided = FALSE,
  distance = "l2",
  method = c("exact", "asymp"),
  k = 1L,
  s = NULL,
  tuning = NULL,
  tuning_mode = c("default", "grid"),
  normalize = TRUE,
  se = TRUE,
  jackknife = c("fast", "loo", "none"),
  denominator_tol = sqrt(.Machine$double.eps),
  row_ids = NULL,
  training = "supplied",
  ctx = NULL,
  return = c("W")
)

Arguments

data

Optional data frame or tibble. Do not combine with X or direct sample vectors.

x_cols

Reporting-covariate columns in data, in target-coordinate order.

y_col, d_col, a_col, e_col

Data-frame columns for outcome, treatment, instrument and instrument propensity.

m_y0_col, m_y1_col

Data-frame outcome predictions by instrument arm.

m_d0_col, m_d1_col

Data-frame treatment predictions by instrument arm. The zero-arm prediction may be omitted with one_sided = TRUE.

X

Numeric reporting matrix, observations in rows.

X0

Numeric target matrix, targets in rows.

x0

Numeric vector for a single target. Supply exactly one of X0,x0.

Y

Finite numeric outcome vector.

D

Numeric binary treatment vector (0/1).

A

Numeric binary instrument vector (0/1).

e

Instrument propensity predictions in \([0,1]\), before clipping.

m_y0, m_y1

Outcome predictions conditional on instrument arm 0 and 1.

m_d0, m_d1

Treatment predictions conditional on instrument arm 0 and 1, in \([0,1]\). m_d0 may be omitted only with one_sided = TRUE.

clip

Propensity clipping threshold in (0,0.5), with 1 - clip < 1 in double precision.

one_sided

Explicit structural restriction that treatment is impossible under instrument 0. Requires D <= A and zero m_d0 if supplied.

distance

Existing distance specification, registered name or function. Geometry is frozen across deletions. Exact distance ties use original covariates lexicographically; identical covariate rows use input position.

method

One of "exact" or "asymp", as in cate_dnn() and np_dnn().

k

Number of neighbors averaged within each size-s subsample, 1 <= k <= s.

s

Deterministic integer order. Covariance requires s < n.

tuning

Optional existing tuning specification, mutually exclusive with s. If neither is provided, the package paper rule resolves the order.

tuning_mode

"default" retains a single fit; "grid" also evaluates feasible tuning candidates using the same frozen signals and ranks.

normalize

Logical normalization control passed to the asymptotic weight rule, as in weights_dnn(). Exact weights are normalized by construction.

se

Whether to compute covariance.

jackknife

"fast" uses the existing prefix/suffix engine; "loo" uses explicit frozen-rank deletions; "none" disables covariance.

denominator_tol

Nonnegative numerical cancellation tolerance. Changes a diagnostic flag only, never the ratio or covariance.

row_ids

Optional aligned unique character/numeric identities.

training

Descriptive declaration: supplied, oracle, full_sample, oob or cross_fit. It is not verified from predictions.

ctx

Optional context passed to the existing distance machinery.

return

Optional extras: W, ranks, ord, dx, ess, signals, deletions, pseudo_values, neighbors or tuning. Unknown values warn and are ignored.

Value

A clate_result inheriting affine_ratio_result. Component roles are reduced_form and first_stage. Optional nuisance output is the complete iv_signals construction record, including raw/used propensity.

Details

The documented sampling framework uses independent observations; cluster and survey-design inference are not supplied. Exact distance ties use lexicographic order of the original covariates, in their supplied column order. Identical covariate rows retain input-order ties; permuting those duplicates can change estimates. Ordering uses no outcomes or nuisances.

Nuisance predictions use all pre-instrument adjustment variables, while weights use the reporting coordinates X. The estimate is the ratio of the adjusted local reduced form and first stage, using common weights.

The accompanying paper gives the IV identifying assumptions and conditions for pointwise inference. A training label or a computational choice of k or weight method does not establish those conditions. Inspect the local first stage alongside the ratio.

Covariance keeps paired variation of both frozen signals. The residualized IV-GMM workflow uses a different moment and can have a different target. Reporting uses the common generics; overlap panels describe the instrument and influence panels retain both augmented signals.

Examples

d <- data.frame(
  x = 1:6, Y = c(1, 2, 0, 3, 2, 1),
  D = c(0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1), A = c(0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1),
  e = rep(.5, 6), y0 = rep(1, 6), y1 = rep(2, 6), d1 = rep(.6, 6)
)
fit <- clate_dnn(
  data = d, x_cols = "x", y_col = "Y", d_col = "D", a_col = "A",
  e_col = "e", m_y0_col = "y0", m_y1_col = "y1", m_d1_col = "d1",
  one_sided = TRUE, x0 = 3, s = 2
)
fit$components
#>        numerator denominator
#> [1,] -0.06666667   0.5733333
fit$theta
#> [1] -0.1162791
clate_dnn(
  X = matrix(d$x, ncol = 1), Y = d$Y, D = d$D, A = d$A,
  e = d$e, m_y0 = d$y0, m_y1 = d$y1, m_d1 = d$d1,
  one_sided = TRUE, x0 = 3, s = 2
)$theta
#> [1] -0.1162791
